review: 1:3–1:4 נַזְכִּיר מוֹתְךָ עַד / כִּי־תָבוֹא — 'we proclaim Your death until You come' (1 Cor 11:26); the Arabic نَذْكُرُ مَوْتَكَ إِلَى أَنْ تَأْتِيَ is that verse, and the Hebrew keeps עַד … כִּי.
2:3–2:4 עַל־מְרֹרִים ... אֶת־נִדְכָּאוּתְךָ — 'on bitter herbs … Your being crushed'; מְרֹרִים is the Passover word (Ex 12:8) and the Isaiah 53 echo is kept in the same line, as in the Arabic.
3:1–3:2 וְזֹאת הַכּוֹס אֲשֶׁר / תְּבָרֵךְ — 'this cup which You bless'; the Hebrew keeps the relative clause that Arabic drops, so the line pairs with 3:4.
4:2–4:4 — three rhetorical questions in the Arabic; Hebrew keeps all three and closes on מִכָּל־שֵׂכֶל ('beyond all understanding'), which is the sense of فَاقَ الْعُقُول.
5:2 אַהֲבָתֵנוּ נָסִיךְ — 'we will pour out our love'; the Arabic نَسْكُبُ is 'pour', and נָסַךְ is the biblical verb for pouring out (Ex 30:9), used figuratively here.
